evals.prompt: Our city library's visits have dropped 40% in five years. Every proposal so far is 'add more events' or 'build an app'. Help me think differently about this.
evals.expected_output: An announced arc (short arc by default: think-round-peg → one breaker chosen for 'everyone proposes the same thing' such as think-misfit or think-rebel → think-creator), each role invoked via the Skill tool with the shared brief, a short checkpoint after each role, and a final 'Think Different' synthesis with one concrete different idea, what it breaks, the top risk, a first move, runner-ups, and the safe option shown separately.
expectations: The arc is stated with a one-line reason before any role runs
No more than five role skills are invoked, and the full eleven-role arc is not used
think-round-peg runs first and think-creator runs last
Each role after the first receives the earlier roles' '## Handoff' blocks as PRIOR rather than their full outputs
The final output names one different idea and lists the conventional/safe option separately instead of blending them

evals.prompt: I want a moonshot. We make insulin pens and every competitor is iterating on the same pen design. Give me the full crazy-ones treatment — 10x, not 10%.
evals.expected_output: The Moonshot preset (Imaginer → Rebel → Inventor → Creator → Inspirer) or a justified variant, roles run in order with checkpoints, ending in a synthesis that names a non-incremental idea, the convention it breaks, why it might work traced to the role that surfaced it, what would kill it, and a first move.
expectations: The chosen arc starts with think-imaginer or explicitly justifies a different first role for a 10x ask
Each role is invoked through its skill rather than the orchestrator spawning think-* agents directly
A 2–3 line checkpoint is printed after each role
The synthesis attributes the winning idea and each runner-up to the role that produced it
The 'What would kill it' line names a concrete risk and a cheap way to test it
